references.text: The people of Israel complained in the same way to Moses and Aaron in the Desert of Sin, accusing them of bringing them out to die of hunger.
The people demanded water at Rephidim and accused Moses of bringing them out of Egypt only to let them die of thirst.
The people complained about their conditions in the wilderness and longed back to Egypt, a recurring complaint against Moses' leadership.
After the report from the spies, the whole congregation complained and asked why the Lord had brought them into this land to fall by the sword.
Dathan and Abiram accused Moses of bringing them out of Egypt only to let them die in the wilderness.
The context for this complaint: the congregation gathered in the Desert of Kadesh where there was no water.
The people complained again against God and Moses about why they had been brought out of Egypt to die in the wilderness.
The expression 'the Lord's assembly' (קְהַל יְהוָה) is used here, referring to the people of Israel who left Egypt.
